newsitem.title: USA: US stocks recoup losses, barely changed at midday.
newsitem.headline: US stocks recoup losses, barely changed at midday.

text.p: U.S. stocks were about unchanged at midday on Tuesday after recouping mild losses sparked by short-selling and profit-taking following yesterday's rally.
The Dow Industrials were off two to 5732 and the Nasdaq Composite Index was up 0.3 to almost 1149 at midsession.

"After a rally like yesterday it's profit-taking, but it also brings out short sellers who are skeptical, who feel 5750 is pretty much a top as we approach it," said Joseph Battiglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal.
On Monday the Dow gained 74 points to 5734.

"We have a good framework now," Battiglia said. "There's great comfort among investors that buying on a dip is still the right strategy and the economy is still on track. Money is still pouring into funds, providing fuel for the fire. Plus, we've had interesting merger proposals..."

Charles Pradillo, market analyst at Cowen & Co, said, "Bonds are weak again. It's a choppy market. The major averages may want to take a run but ... bonds make it difficult. Plus, with Fed officials saying inflation is worrisome, it's very confusing and worrisome for the market."
On Monday the Nasdaq and Russell 2000 indices did not match the gains of the Dow and the S&P 500 Index on a percentage basis.
ITT Corp shares were under seige after the company warned that third quarter results would fall below forecasts due to weak gaming revenue, particularly at its Las Vegas operations.
ITT topped the New York Stock Exchange percentage losers list in extremely heavy trading. The shares were off 7-7/8, or about 15 percent, to 48-1/8.
Shares of the Big Three U.S. automakers fell after Ford Motor Co disclosed that its financial performance in Brazil in the 1996 second half would be "substantially worse" than the first half.
Ford shares were down one to 30-1/4 in heavy trading.

General Motors Corp, which also has substantial Brazilian operations, fell 7/8 to 47-3/8, and Chrysler Corp, which recently announced a $315 million plan for its first Brazilian assembly plant, dropped 3/4 at 28.
